answer.rationale: Finance demands 18% spend cut; incumbent won't move on price (memory_c6 shows multi-year leverage is exhausted this cycle). The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate (memory_c2 confirms prior switch was operationally clean — quick onboarding, accurate invoicing). With 14 days to expiry and no auto-renew, inaction becomes a forced stop. The assembly line is at 94% with no buffer, so I am not adding a second source (would split volume, reduce savings) and not deferring (contract lapses). Before committing, I pull memory_c2 to re-confirm onboarding timeline fits the 14-day window and memory_c4 to verify whether a final benchmarking call could extract any concession from the incumbent as a walk-away fallback. If both checks hold, I switch the primary supply contract to the low-cost vendor at the quoted price, structured as a 12-month term with delivery SLA penalties to protect the 94%-utilization line. The incumbent relationship is preserved for a future cycle; the non-critical renewal deferred last cycle (memory_c5) remains month-to-month and stays deferred.
